Read-only review (Opus). Not built here.

Verdict: Needs changes before merge.

The PR merges cleanly with `origin/main` (`git merge-tree`, no conflict). The `Project:` line is correct now. But the URL that the Report door sends can still contain a directory path of the user. Two leaks stay.

## Blockers

1. `crates/ui/src/egui_app/debug_info.rs:94-99` - the `Status:` line still sends full paths. The shared form replaces only the exact project path. Many status texts put a different full path into `state.status`:
   - `crates/ui/src/state.rs:4554` - `open failed: {}: {err}` with `path.display()`. Here the failed path is not `project_path`, so no replacement occurs. This is the usual case where a user files a bug.
   - `crates/ui/src/state.rs:4717` - machined stock `written to {}`.
   - `crates/ui/src/state_fixture_library.rs:149`, `crates/ui/src/state_fixture_profile.rs:348`, `crates/ui/src/state_setup_post_options.rs:229`, `crates/ui/src/state_tool_library.rs:59` - `written to` / `to {}` with `path.display()`.

   The PR body lists this under "Not exercised", and the decision drops a general scrub. But issue #2744 asks that the door sends no directory part, and these texts send one. Required: the shared form must not carry a directory path from the status. Acceptable ways:
   - change these status texts to the file name (the import texts already use `file_label`), or
   - in `shared_report`, replace each path-like token of the status with its last segment, or
   - in `shared_report`, write a fixed word for the status when it has a path separator.

   Add a test: `project_path = None`, `status = "open failed: <user path>: ..."`, and assert that the body and the URL do not contain the directory or the user name.

2. `crates/ui/src/egui_app/debug_info.rs:51-54` - `file_name_only` uses `Path::file_name`, which reads only the separators of the running system. On Linux and macOS, `Path::new(r"C:\Users\jane\m.json").file_name()` gives the full string, because `\` is not a separator there. The machine path comes from the project file (`machine::of`, stored at the save). Thus a project that was saved on Windows and opened on Linux or macOS sends the full Windows path of the machine file. Required: take the last segment after `/` or `\` on all systems, and ignore trailing separators. Add a test that runs on each system with the two forms (`C:\Users\jane.doe\Parts\m.json` and `/home/jane.doe/Parts/m.json`). The current test uses only the form of the running system (`cfg!(windows)`).

## Notes (no change required)

- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` in the new code. `to_string_lossy` gives a defined result for non-UTF-8 parts. A root or `..` gives `(no file name)`. An unsaved project gives `Project: unsaved`.
- A trailing separator (`...\Parts\`) gives the last directory name (`Parts`). That is one directory name, not a full path. After blocker 2, make sure that the result is defined and is the same on all systems.
- Layering: the change uses only `camcraft_app` API functions that the file used before (`machine::of`, `units::of`). No `sys_*` or world-level calls are new.
- The look of the dialog does not change. Only the data of the URL changes. Thus no screenshots are necessary.
- The pinning test `the_report_door_url_has_the_project_file_name_and_no_directory` asserts the absence of the directory, the home, the user name and `Parts`, as typed and percent-encoded. This is good. It also asserts that the in-app report keeps the full path.
- The tests are in the `camcraft-ui` lib (`report_tests.rs`), next to the code. No snapshot PNG changes. File lengths: `debug_info.rs` 121, `report.rs` 237, `report_tests.rs` 246 lines.
- The body is complete: `Changelog:` line, `Fixes` line, quick gate on head `e6565e1fd` with the test names, and a decision file.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Addressed (head fa7d1b7552b460e65f269904da1faa41c0caab55).

1. Blocker 1 (`Status:` line with other paths): fixed at the report builder. `debug_info::shared_report` now passes the whole report text through `report_scrub::scrub_paths`. Each path-like word in each field changes to its last component. This includes the status, the GPU line, the machine vendor and model, the machine file and the project. Windows drive and UNC forms, POSIX forms, `~` forms, relative forms and folder names with spaces are covered. The status strip and the in-app Debug info do not change. The exact-path replace of the first form is removed. Pin: `report_tests::the_report_door_scrubs_a_status_path_that_is_not_the_project` (no saved project; Windows and POSIX `open failed:` paths; body and URL, typed and percent-encoded, have `part.camproj` and no `someone`, `secret` or `Documents`). Unit pin: `report_scrub::tests::scrub_paths_keeps_only_the_file_name_of_each_path`.
2. Blocker 2 (`file_name_only` on Linux and macOS): `file_name_only` now uses `report_scrub::last_component`. It reads `/` and `\` on every system. A trailing separator gives the last folder name. A root, a drive, `.` or `..` gives `(no file name)`. A non-UTF-8 name reads lossily. Pin: `report_scrub::tests::last_component_reads_both_separators_on_every_system` (`C:\Users\jane.doe\Parts\m.json` and `/home/jane.doe/Parts/m.json`, the same asserts on each system; no `cfg!`).

`origin/main` is merged in (merge commit, no conflict). On the merged tree: `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib --locked` gives 1290 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` is clean. The look of the dialog does not change. The decision file and the PR body are updated.

<!-- pr-reviewer: fa7d1b7552b460e65f269904da1faa41c0caab55 -->
Read-only delta review (Opus). Not built here.

Scope: the commits after the reviewed head `e6565e1fd`: `96afea412` and the merge `fa7d1b755`.

Verdict: Needs changes before merge.

The earlier change request stays open. Blocker 2 of the first review (`file_name_only` on Linux and macOS) is resolved. Blocker 1 is resolved for most texts, but one class of folder names still leaks.

## Blockers

1. `crates/ui/src/egui_app/report_scrub.rs:86` and `:91` - a stop mark inside a folder name ends the path too early. The part of the path before the mark goes to GitHub.
   - Input: `open failed: C:\Users\jane\OneDrive - Contoso, Ltd\Parts\x.camproj: access denied`
   - Output: `open failed: OneDrive - Contoso, x.camproj: access denied`
   - Input: `saved /home/jane/ACME (old) parts/x.camproj`
   - Output: `saved ACME (old) x.camproj`
   - The word `Contoso,` ends with `,`, and the word `(old)` ends with `)`. Thus `ends_path` stops the scan. The organization or customer name in the folder survives. A OneDrive for Business folder is named `OneDrive - <organization>`, and Windows often moves `Documents` into it. Thus each project path on such a computer goes through that folder. Folder names such as `Smith, John` or `Copy (2) of parts` give the same result.
   - The decision file says "A scrub that guesses wrong can only shorten good text; it cannot send a directory". This is not true for these inputs.
   - Required change: a stop mark must not end the path while a later word on the same line has a separator. One leak-free rule: run the path to the last later word on the line that has a separator, and use the stop mark only to find the trailing marks of that last word. The cost is that two paths on one line merge into the last file name. That only shortens the text, and it sends no directory.
   - Add the two inputs above to `scrub_paths_keeps_only_the_file_name_of_each_path`. Expected: `open failed: x.camproj: access denied` and `saved x.camproj`.

## Sample texts (worked by hand against `scrub_paths`)

- `open failed: C:\Users\jane doe\My Parts\part.camproj: access denied` -> `open failed: part.camproj: access denied`. No directory.
- `saved /home/jane/work dir/a b.camproj` -> `saved a b.camproj`. No directory.
- `open failed: \server\share\jane\x.step` -> `open failed: x.step`. No directory.
- `C:/Users/jane/x.camproj` -> `x.camproj`.
- `"C:\Users\jane\x.camproj" not found` -> `"x.camproj" not found`.
- `file:///C:/Users/jane/x.camproj` -> `x.camproj`. The scheme is removed too.
- `~/secret/x.nc` -> `x.nc`.
- `..\jane\x.camproj` -> `x.camproj`.
- `post written to D:\out\jane's parts\p.nc (12 kB)` -> `post written to p.nc (12 kB)`.
- A path followed by `.` or `,` (`saved /home/jane/x.camproj, 3 ops`) -> `saved x.camproj, 3 ops`. The mark stays.
- `C:\Users\jane` -> `jane`. See note 1.
- Two paths on one line (`copied /a/b/x.nc to /c/d/y.nc`) -> `copied y.nc`. No directory, but the first name and `to` are lost.
- Non-ASCII (`C:\Users\jörg\Teile\teil.camproj`) -> `teil.camproj`. The slices are safe.
- `feed 300 mm/min at 1/2 depth` -> unchanged.
- `https://example.com/a/b` -> `b`. The host and the scheme are lost. No leak.
- Folder name with `, ` or a word that ends with `)` -> leaks. Blocker 1.

## Checks that pass

- `git show --remerge-diff fa7d1b755` is empty. The merge is class SAME.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main origin/issue/2744-report-door-file-name` is clean.
- `debug_info::shared_report` scrubs the whole report text after the build. No field skips the scrub: version, GPU, project, machine vendor, model and file, document, frame rate and status. The scrub works line by line, so a path cannot run into the next line.
- `report::report_body` embeds only `shared_report`. `issue_url` percent-encodes that body. Thus the URL uses only the scrubbed text.
- `last_component` reads `/` and `\` on each system. The edge cases keep their defined results: an unsaved project gives `Project: unsaved`; a root, a drive, `.`, `..` and an empty string give `(no file name)`; a trailing separator gives the last folder name; a non-UTF-8 name reads lossily.
- Panic safety: no `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` outside tests. Each byte-index slice (`split_at(body_start)`, `rest[body.len()..]`, `joined[lead.len()..]`) cuts at an ASCII mark or at a prefix length, so it is on a char boundary. `starts_path` reads `b[0..3]` only after a length check. An empty string and a lone `"` give empty bodies and no panic. Each loop is bounded: `i` increases in each pass.
- The three new tests prove what their names say. None of them covers blocker 1.
- File lengths: `report_scrub.rs` 149, `debug_info.rs` 113, `report_tests.rs` 270. The changes stay in `camcraft-ui` and use no `sys_*` or world calls.
- The look of the dialog does not change, and the PR body says so. No screenshots are necessary.
- The `Addressed` comment reports `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib --locked` on the merged tree (1290 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored) and a clean clippy.

## Notes (not blockers)

1. A path to a folder keeps its last folder name (`C:\Users\jane` -> `jane`). This is the defined rule. No status text of the application names a home folder today. A new status that names a folder must keep this in mind.
2. A word with two or more `/` that is not a path shrinks to its last part. Examples: a URL, a date `2026/11/20`, or an OpenGL renderer text such as `GTX 1060/PCIe/SSE2` on the `GPU:` line (-> `SSE2`). This loses triage data but sends nothing private. A rule that skips `GPU:` and `CamCraft`/`Build`/`Source commit` lines is optional.
3. A relative path with no root, a space in its first folder and one `/` (`jane doe/x.nc`) keeps its first word. The PR body says so. The application does not make this form.

Addressed (head fa6d90ac579d910356757d6c29cc0bb132e24ee8).

Delta-review blocker (`report_scrub.rs:86` and `:91`, a mark inside a folder name ends the path): fixed. The stop marks are removed. A path now runs to the last later word of the same line that has a separator. A reason after the path has no separator, so it stays. Two paths on one line merge into the last file name.

New inputs in `report_scrub::tests::scrub_paths_keeps_only_the_file_name_of_each_path`, with their outputs:
- `open failed: C:\Users\jane\OneDrive - Contoso, Ltd\Parts\x.camproj: access denied` -> `open failed: x.camproj: access denied`
- `saved /home/jane/ACME (old) parts/x.camproj` -> `saved x.camproj`
- `saved C:\Users\jane\Shop; north\x.camproj` -> `saved x.camproj`
- `written to /home/jane/"Shop" files/x.nc` -> `written to x.nc`

The earlier results stay: `...part.camproj: not found` keeps its reason, and `feed 1200 mm/min, ok` does not change.

The decision file no longer says that a wrong guess "cannot send a directory". It states the rule and its known limits: a path to a folder keeps the last folder name; a relative path without a root keeps its first word; a non-path text with two `/` (for example a GPU text) shrinks.

`origin/main` is merged in (merge commit, no conflict). On the merged tree: `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib --locked` gives 1290 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` is clean.

Read-only delta review (Opus). Not built here.

Scope: the commits after `fa7d1b755`: `4fbd4922a` and the merge `fa6d90ac5`.

Verdict for the whole PR at this head: Ready to merge.

This verdict replaces the earlier verdicts (head `e6565e1fd` and head `fa7d1b755`). It withdraws the change request of those reviews. All three blockers are resolved.

## The blocker of the last review

`scrub_line` (`report_scrub.rs`) no longer stops a path at a mark. A path now runs to the last word of the line that has a separator. The output is the part after the last separator of that word. Thus each word between the start of the path and that word is removed, and no folder name before the last separator survives.

- `open failed: C:\Users\jane\OneDrive - Contoso, Ltd\Parts\x.camproj: access denied` -> `open failed: x.camproj: access denied`
- `saved /home/jane/ACME (old) parts/x.camproj` -> `saved x.camproj`

## Sample texts (worked by hand against the new rule)

- `open failed: C:\Users\jane doe\My Parts\part.camproj: access denied` -> `open failed: part.camproj: access denied`
- `saved /home/jane/work dir/a b.camproj` -> `saved a b.camproj`
- `open failed: \server\share\jane\x.step` -> `open failed: x.step`
- `C:/Users/jane/x.camproj` -> `x.camproj`
- `"C:\Users\jane\x.camproj" not found` -> `"x.camproj" not found`
- `file:///C:/Users/jane/x.camproj` -> `x.camproj`
- `~/secret/x.nc` -> `x.nc`
- `..\jane\x.camproj` -> `x.camproj`
- `post written to D:\out\jane's parts\p.nc (12 kB)` -> `post written to p.nc (12 kB)`
- `saved /home/jane/x.camproj, 3 ops` -> `saved x.camproj, 3 ops`
- `C:\Users\jane` -> `jane` (the defined rule for a folder; see note 2)
- `copied /a/b/x.nc to /c/d/y.nc` -> `copied y.nc`
- `C:\Users\jörg\Teile\teil.camproj` -> `teil.camproj`
- `feed 300 mm/min at 1/2 depth` -> unchanged
- `https://example.com/a/b` -> `b`
- `saved C:\Users\jane\x.camproj at 300 mm/min` -> `saved min`. The file name and the prose are lost. Nothing private stays.
- `open failed: C:\Users\jane\x.camproj (see docs/help)` -> `open failed: help)`. The file name and the prose are lost. Nothing private stays.
- An empty line -> an empty line. An empty text stays empty.
- `/` -> `(no file name)`. `\ //` -> one space. No panic.

## Checks that pass

- `git show --remerge-diff fa6d90ac5` is empty. The merge is class SAME.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main origin/issue/2744-report-door-file-name` is clean.
- Panic safety: `(i..words.len()).rev().find(..).unwrap_or(i)` cannot panic. Each word that starts a path has a separator, so `end >= i` always. The slice `joined[lead.len()..]` cuts after ASCII marks at the start of `words[i]`, which is also the start of `joined`. Thus it is on a char boundary. The loop is bounded: `i` increases in each pass.
- The unit test `scrub_paths_keeps_only_the_file_name_of_each_path` has the two inputs of the last review and three more (`Shop; north`, a quoted `"Shop"` folder, and `C:/` with a reason). The earlier inputs still hold by hand.
- The decision file no longer says "cannot send a directory". It states the rule and its known limits.
- `report_scrub.rs` has 142 lines. The change stays in `camcraft-ui`.
- The PR body says that the look of the dialog does not change.
- The `Addressed` comment reports `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib --locked` on the merged tree (1290 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored) and a clean clippy.

## Notes (not blockers)

1. A word with a separator later on the line takes the file name with it (`at 300 mm/min`, `(see docs/help)`). The report then names no file. This loses triage data and sends nothing private. If a status text of this form is found, a later change can stop a path at a word with only one `/` that does not start a path.
2. A path to a folder keeps its last folder name. A relative path without a root keeps its first word. The decision file names both limits.
